workspace.trellis:title: Good Syllabus Design
workspace.trellis:description: A syllabus ontology that encodes what separates working syllabi from drawer-fillers: contract plus map, checkable objectives, transparent grading, humane policies, and honest workload.

syllabus-schema.description: The syllabus as contract and map — answers why before what, signals course character, and stays usable as a reference all term.

fields.name: courseCode
fields.description: Short identifier (e.g. CS 301, DES-420)

fields.name: term
fields.description: When the course runs (e.g. Fall 2026)

fields.name: framing
fields.description: Why should I care? Big questions the course wrestles with — before policies and mechanics.

fields.name: capabilities
fields.description: What you'll walk away able to do — concrete capability, not vague 'understanding'.

fields.name: courseCharacter
fields.description: What this course values — if you deleted the title, could someone still tell what kind of course this is?

fields.name: weeklyHours
fields.description: Honest expected hours per week (reading + assignments + class)

fields.name: objectives
fields.description: Concrete, checkable learning objectives

fields.name: modules
fields.description: Week-by-week or module structure showing sequencing logic

fields.name: gradingComponents
fields.description: Transparent, effort-proportional grading breakdown

fields.name: policies
fields.description: Humane policies that set expectations without copy-pasted legal armor

fields.name: totalGradingWeight
fields.description: Should sum to 100% — sanity check for transparent grading

learning-objective-schema.description: A concrete, checkable learning objective — verifiable by instructor and student, not vibes.

fields.name: statement
fields.description: Observable outcome (e.g. 'Run and interpret a t-test on a real dataset')

fields.name: checkable
fields.description: Can progress be verified without relying on subjective judgment alone?

fields.name: verificationMethod
fields.description: How instructor and student confirm this objective was met

course-module-schema.description: A course unit whose placement reveals the logic of the course — why this comes before that.

fields.name: sequenceNumber
fields.description: Week or module order

fields.name: buildsOn
fields.description: Prior units this module depends on — makes sequencing logic explicit

fields.name: topics
fields.description: Scannable summary — usable as a reference mid-term

fields.name: readingLoad
fields.description: Estimated reading hours this unit

fields.name: assignmentLoad
fields.description: Estimated assignment hours this unit

grading-component-schema.description: A graded component with transparent weight proportional to effort and cognitive load.

fields.name: weight
fields.description: Share of final grade — should track actual time and effort

fields.name: effortHours
fields.description: Realistic hours expected for this component

fields.name: description
fields.description: What is being evaluated — no vague 'participation' without a rubric

fields.name: rubric
fields.description: Optional link to a rubric when grading criteria need to be legible

course-policy-schema.description: A humane policy that sets expectations and acknowledges real edge cases.

fields.name: summary
fields.description: One-line scannable rule — for 'what's the late policy again?' moments

fields.name: fullText
fields.description: Complete policy language

fields.name: edgeCases
fields.description: How illness, emergencies, and other real situations are handled

nodes.trellis:title: Local-First Systems Design
nodes.trellis:description: Example syllabus demonstrating good syllabus design principles
nodes.framing: How do you build software that keeps working when the network doesn't? This course wrestles with local-first architecture, semantic data models, and the design choices that make systems feel owned rather than rented.
nodes.capabilities: Design and prototype a local-first workspace with explicit ontology, typed queries, and offline-capable sync — and articulate tradeoffs against cloud-default patterns.

nodes.trellis:title: Interpret statistical tests on real data
nodes.statement: Be able to run and interpret a t-test on a real dataset, including stating assumptions and limitations.
nodes.verificationMethod: Lab submission with annotated output and written interpretation checked against a rubric.

nodes.trellis:title: Design a domain ontology
nodes.statement: Define a Trellis schema for a novel domain with distinct entity types, relations, and at least one computed field.
nodes.verificationMethod: Peer review against a checklist: non-overlapping types, checkable fields, explicit relations.

nodes.trellis:title: Articulate sync tradeoffs
nodes.statement: Compare CRDT, op-log, and last-write-wins strategies for a given use case in a written memo.
nodes.verificationMethod: Memo graded on named tradeoffs, not vague 'understanding'.

nodes.trellis:title: Foundations: Files, Graphs, and Ownership
nodes.topics: Filesystem vs graph models; EAV basics; why local-first matters

nodes.trellis:title: Ontology Design
nodes.topics: Schema design; relations and rollups; checkable objectives as schema fields

nodes.trellis:title: Sync and Conflict
nodes.topics: Op-logs; peer sync; conflict semantics — builds on ontology from week 2

nodes.trellis:title: Studio Projects
nodes.description: Three iterative prototypes with peer critique. Weight reflects sustained design + implementation effort.

nodes.trellis:title: Weekly Labs
nodes.description: Checkable skill exercises with explicit verification criteria per lab.

nodes.trellis:title: Studio Participation
nodes.description: Prepared critique of peer work in at least 8 of 10 sessions. Rubric defines 'prepared' — not attendance alone.

nodes.trellis:title: Final Reflection Memo
nodes.description: Synthesis of design choices across the term — what you'd do differently and why.

nodes.trellis:title: Late Work Policy
nodes.summary: 48-hour grace window, then 10% per day; extensions by request before deadline.
nodes.fullText: Assignments submitted within 48 hours of the deadline receive full credit. After that, 10% deducted per calendar day. Request extensions before the deadline for illness or emergencies — no documentation required for first request.
nodes.edgeCases: Illness and family emergencies: email before deadline, we'll find a path. Chronic situations: talk to me in week 1 so we can plan.

nodes.trellis:title: Collaboration & Integrity
nodes.summary: Collaborate on ideas; submit your own work; cite AI assistance.
nodes.fullText: Discuss concepts freely. Code and written submissions must be your own unless a group assignment says otherwise. If you use AI tools, note where and how in your submission.
nodes.edgeCases: Unsure if something counts as collaboration? Ask before submitting — not after.

checkable-objectives.description: Objectives that pass the checkable test
checkable-objectives.eqls: FIND root AS ?r WHERE ?r.workspace.graph.nodes.@type = 'LearningObjective' AND ?r.workspace.graph.nodes.checkable = true RETURN ?r.workspace.graph.nodes.statement

grading-weight-check.natural_language: Do all grading components for this syllabus sum to 100% weight?
